title: Hockey India Announces Rs 50 Lakh Reward for Women's Team After Best World Cup Finish in 52 Years
excerpt: Each player receives Rs 2 lakh as the federation celebrates India's historic fifth-place result at the 2026 FIH Women's Hockey World Cup in the Netherlands.
body:
• Hockey India announced Rs 50 lakh in cash awards for the women's team after their historic fifth-place finish at the FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 in the Netherlands.
  • Each player will receive Rs 2 lakh and each support staff member Rs 1 lakh, with the total award recognizing the team's best World Cup result in 52 years.
  • Captain Salima Tete led India to just one defeat in the entire tournament, including a 3-1 win over Germany in the classification match.
  • The team now shifts focus to the Asian Games, where Hockey India hopes the World Cup momentum will carry forward.

Hockey India Announces Rs 50 Lakh Cash Award

Hockey India has announced a cash award of Rs 50 lakh for the Indian women's hockey team following their fifth-place finish at the FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 in Amstelveen, the Netherlands. The result marks India's best performance at the tournament in 52 years — since the team finished fourth at the inaugural World Cup in 1974.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2093413943293432053

Each player will receive Rs 2 lakh, while every member of the coaching and support staff will get Rs 1 lakh, according to a statement from the federation.

"To finish fifth at a World Cup after 52 years is a testament to the hard work, resilience and fighting spirit of this team."

— Dr Dilip Tirkey, President, Hockey India

A Tournament of Resilience

Under captain Salima Tete and chief coach Sjoerd Marijne, India suffered just one defeat across the entire tournament. The team held powerhouses China, England, and Australia to draws, beat South Africa 6-1 in the group stage, and closed the campaign with a dominant 3-1 victory over Germany in the fifth/sixth classification match.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3J0eeIZvdPI

The consistency was notable. India did not collapse in any game and competed toe-to-toe with teams ranked well above them, a marked departure from previous World Cup campaigns where group-stage exits were the norm.

Looking Ahead to the Asian Games

Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh praised the squad and said the federation hopes the World Cup performance will serve as a springboard for the upcoming Asian Games. "This is a proud moment for Indian hockey," Singh said, according to NDTV. "We hope this achievement motivates the team to aim even higher at the Asian Games."

The Asian Games hold particular significance for Indian women's hockey. A strong finish there would further solidify the team's standing in international competition and potentially improve their ranking heading into the next Olympic cycle.

Growing Profile of Indian Women's Hockey

The World Cup campaign adds to a growing list of breakthrough moments for Indian women's hockey. The team's fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 was a watershed, drawing unprecedented public attention to the sport. The fifth-place World Cup finish — their best since the tournament's inception — suggests the progress is durable rather than a one-off result.

For the Indian diaspora, the team's run in the Netherlands drew significant viewership and social media engagement. Women's hockey has become one of the more visible Indian team sports globally, with players like Tete, goalkeeper Savita Punia, and drag-flicker Deep Grace Ekka earning recognition beyond traditional hockey-following audiences.

What's Next

The immediate focus shifts to Asian Games preparation. Marijne's coaching tenure, which has now delivered two historic results — the Olympic semifinal and the World Cup fifth place — will be under scrutiny as the team seeks to convert near-misses into medals. The Rs 50 lakh award, while modest by some standards, signals that Hockey India views this squad as one worth investing in for the long term.
